description: Patients who have at least one lab record with a recorded RA result other than '-'.

a.request: Among patients with at least one laboratory record whose rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result is recorded and is something other than '-', list the 10 with the highest average hematocrit (`HCT`) across all their lab records. Show patient `ID`, average uric acid (`UA`) and average hematocrit, highest hematocrit first, with patients who have no hematocrit values last. Averages ignore missing values. Don't round.
a.sql: SELECT ID, AVG(UA) AS avg_UA, AVG(HCT) AS avg_HCT FROM Laboratory WHERE ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RA IS NOT NULL AND RA <> '-') GROUP BY ID ORDER BY (AVG(HCT) IS NULL), AVG(HCT) DESC LIMIT 10

b.request: Select the 10 patients having at least one lab record with a non-null `RA` value other than '-', and report each one's `ID`, average `UA` and average `HCT` computed over all of their lab records (ignoring nulls, unrounded), ordered by average `HCT` descending with patients having no `HCT` values last.
b.sql: SELECT ID, AVG(UA) AS avg_UA, AVG(HCT) AS avg_HCT FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN RA IS NOT NULL AND RA <> '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 ORDER BY (AVG(HCT) IS NULL), AVG(HCT) DESC, ID LIMIT 10
b.raw: Select the 10 patients having at least one lab record with a non-null `RA` value other than '-', and report each one's `ID`, average `UA` and average `HCT` computed over all of their lab records (ignoring nulls, unrounded), ordered by average `HCT` descending with patients having no `HCT` values last.

c.request: Looking only at patients without a rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result of '-' in their lab tests, which 10 have the highest average hematocrit (`HCT`) across all their lab records? Show patient `ID`, average uric acid (`UA`) and average hematocrit, highest first, with patients who have no hematocrit values last. Ignore missing values in the averages and don't round. Patients who have at least one lab record with a recorded RA result other than '-'.
c.sql: SELECT ID, AVG(UA) AS avg_ua, AVG(HCT) AS avg_hct FROM Laboratory WHERE ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RA IS NOT NULL AND RA <> '-') GROUP BY ID ORDER BY (AVG(HCT) IS NULL), AVG(HCT) DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: Among patients who have at least one lab record with a non-null `RA` value other than '-', find the 10 with the highest average `HCT` across all of their lab records (including those where `RA` is '-'), showing `ID`, average `UA` and average `HCT`, ordered by average `HCT` descending with patients having no `HCT` values last, ignoring NULLs in the averages and not rounding.
d.sql: SELECT ID, AVG(UA) AS avg_UA, AVG(HCT) AS avg_HCT FROM Laboratory WHERE ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RA IS NOT NULL AND RA <> '-') GROUP BY ID ORDER BY (AVG(HCT) IS NULL) ASC, AVG(HCT) DESC LIMIT 10
